_note: Hand-entered county posture records. Not a scrape. Every record was read from the linked source before it was typed, and the FIPS code was checked against the Census 2020 national county file. A record with a date I could not pin down is either left out or marked confidence: medium with the uncertainty stated in the note. Where the restrictive action was taken by a city or town rather than the county, moratorium is false and the municipal action is described in the note - a parcel elsewhere in the county is not covered by a city ordinance, and pretending otherwise would produce a wrong answer for the majority of the county's land.
coverage: 27 counties. Chosen for signal, not for national coverage: the ones with a documented moratorium, denial or ordinance change since 2024, plus a handful of permissive ones for contrast. Anything not in this file falls back to no county-level blocker known, which is an absence of evidence and is labelled as such by ingest/counties.py.

records.moratorium_note: No county-wide moratorium, but on 7 July 2026 the Board of Supervisors voted 8-0 to deny the comprehensive plan amendment for Dulles Cloud South, a ~1,940-acre, 43 million sq ft campus that would have been the largest in county history. The vote came days after the Prince William Digital Gateway collapsed.
records.board_history: Digital Gateway rezoning approved 2023 under the prior board, then unwound; Dulles Cloud South denied unanimously 7 Jul 2026 with county staff recommending denial on infrastructure, traffic and rural-character grounds. Two consecutive board postures, opposite directions - do not price this county off the 2023 vote.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. The Board of Supervisors voted 4-3 at its 27 May 2026 meeting (reported 28 May) to deny the rezoning, the building-height special exception and the substation conditional use permit for Tract's 430-acre Mountain Road Technology Park.
records.board_history: Denial came after a near-six-hour hearing and survived proffers of $15M for water infrastructure and $6M for parkland. A 4-3 split means one seat decides the next one; treat this as contested rather than settled.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. On 18 March 2025 the Board of Supervisors voted 7-2 to amend the zoning ordinance so data centers are a special exception use in districts where they had been by-right. Applications filed before 12 February 2025 and more than 500 ft from housing were grandfathered if diligently pursued without substantial modification.
records.board_history: 7-2 with Umstattd and Kershner dissenting. Phase 2 of the standards-and-locations work program was approved 16 Sep 2025 and is still open, so the rules can tighten again. The county that invented by-right data center zoning has removed it.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. Louisa created Technology Overlay Districts in 2023 covering roughly 6,000 acres near high-voltage transmission, and approved AWS's Lake Anna and North Creek campuses against an announced $11B investment through 2040.
records.board_history: Permissive inside the overlay, not outside it. AWS withdrew a 7.2 million sq ft third campus in late July 2025 after public opposition over water, traffic and rural identity - the overlay is a welcome mat with a size limit on it.

records.moratorium_note: Expedited Bill 19-26, adopted 28 July 2026, bars the Department of Permitting Services from issuing any data center permit for 18 months. It reaches applications filed before the effective date, applications pending review, and approvals that have not yet had a building permit issued.
records.board_history: Passed alongside ZTA 26-01, which redefines data centers and prohibits hyperscale facilities in the county for now. Council President Fani-Gonzalez framed it as buying time to write guardrails, so expect standards rather than a permanent ban when it lapses.

records.moratorium_note: County Council approved a two-year moratorium on hyperscale data center development on 7 July 2026, the longest pause in Maryland. It can be lifted early if the county adopts a zoning framework setting where data centers may go and on what conditions.
records.board_history: Grew out of the fight over a hyperscale proposal at the shuttered Landover Mall, which produced a county data center task force. Council member Tim Adams voted no, on the two-year length rather than the principle.

records.moratorium_note: On 1 July 2026 the Board of Supervisors imposed an 18-month moratorium on new applications to rezone into the EU-3 Large-Scale Data Center district, effective immediately through 11:59pm on 1 January 2028. Unincorporated Linn County only - it does not bind Cedar Rapids or the other incorporated cities.
records.board_history: Passed 2-1 with Supervisor Sami Scheetz against, four months after the same board unanimously adopted the EU-3 ordinance on 18 February 2026 (1,000 ft residential setbacks, mandatory water study, noise and light limits). They wrote the district, then froze it.

records.moratorium_note: The Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on 14 July 2026 for a one-year (365-day) moratorium on data center construction, extending a 45-day emergency moratorium adopted in June 2026. Applications are still accepted and processed; permits are not issued.
records.board_history: Unanimous. An advisory board is to deliver zoning and building policy by January 2027, and county counsel has said the land-use rules could change as a result. Public health and resource demand were the stated drivers.

records.moratorium_note: The Board of County Commissioners unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium on data centers and related infrastructure on unincorporated county land on 9 June 2026, and started forming an advisory committee to recommend permanent regulations.
records.board_history: Two unanimous votes a month apart - 12 May 2026 to open the process, 9 June 2026 to adopt. Driven by opposition to Green Data's proposed 10,000-acre data center and solar array with New Mexico Tech.

records.moratorium_note: The Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously on 2 July 2026 for an 18-month moratorium on data center development, and lowered the trigger from the proposed 100 MW to 1 MW so that nearly any facility falls under county review while permanent standards are written.
records.board_history: Sponsored by Commissioners Cacari Stone and Hughes; the term was extended from 12 to 18 months and the threshold cut by two orders of magnitude during the hearing. There were no pending proposals - this is pre-emptive, which is the harder posture to negotiate against.

records.moratorium_note: Commissioners enacted a permanent ban on data centers effective immediately on 20 April 2026, replacing the one-year moratorium already in place. Reported as the first outright county ban in Indiana.
records.board_history: Same ordinance also put strict limits on solar and battery storage. Marshall was the first mover in a wave: Indiana University's Environmental Resilience Institute counted 11 Indiana counties with data center ordinances and at least 17 with temporary moratoria by mid-2026.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. Commissioners voted 5-1 to deny Project Tango, an AI data center in rural Loxahatchee, without prejudice, after a 12-hour hearing (reported 16 July 2026). Mayor Sara Baxter recused herself on advice of the County Attorney because of prior public statements in a quasi-judicial matter.
records.board_history: Denied on compatibility, noise, water and traffic. Note the asymmetry: the same commission had already approved the 202-acre Central Park Commerce Center on the site, and those entitlements survive the denial. A denial here is project-specific, not a land ban.

records.moratorium_note: Commissioners voted on 9 July 2026 to halt acceptance, review and approval of hyperscale data center applications until at least July 2027. Hyperscale follows the state definition of 50 MW or more, so sub-50 MW facilities are outside the freeze.
records.board_history: One of a cluster of Florida county pauses in July 2026. The 50 MW line is the thing to design against - it is a threshold, not a ban, and it interacts directly with how a project phases its generation.

records.moratorium_note: A moratorium on data center applications has been in place since July 2025. On 9 June 2026 the Commission voted 5-2 to extend it another 100 days, through 30 September 2026.
records.board_history: The moratorium exists to buy time for an ordinance the commission keeps not passing: on 23 June 2026 it deferred the land use and zoning ordinance 5-2 to 11 August. Draft would confine data centers to industrial areas and require a special land use permit in most cases. Assume further extensions.

records.moratorium_note: The Board of Commissioners approved a temporary moratorium on data centers, announced by the county on 10 July 2026.
records.board_history: Announced on the county's own site. Duration and expiry were not stated in the announcement, so treat the end date as unknown and confirm with the county before relying on it.

records.moratorium_note: No county-level moratorium. The restrictive action was municipal: the City of Fayetteville passed a 90-day moratorium on data center applications at its January 2026 work session, then amended its Unified Development Ordinance on 5 March 2026 so data centers are no longer a permitted use inside city limits. Unincorporated Fayette County is not covered.
records.board_history: The QTS campus on 615 acres in Fayetteville was the first hyperscale campus to break ground in Georgia, in 2023; three years later the same city wrote the use out of its code. A developer appeal was withdrawn in March 2026.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. Glynn County commissioners rejected a proposed data center moratorium in April 2026 despite organised community pushback, and moved ahead on zoning rules instead.
records.board_history: Included as a counterweight to the Georgia cluster: opposition showing up at a hearing does not mean the board follows. A screen that treats organised opposition as a proxy for a denial will be wrong here.

records.moratorium_note: An 18-month pause on data centers took effect 7 July 2026 in the consolidated City and County of Broomfield.
records.board_history: Broomfield is a consolidated city-county, so the municipal action and the county action are the same action - one of the few places where a city ordinance does bind the whole FIPS.

records.moratorium_note: Moratorium adopted then withdrawn. The county adopted a one-year moratorium on 12 May 2026 and rescinded it on 5 June 2026 in the face of a reported $100 million developer lawsuit, replacing it with an applicant requirements checklist.
records.board_history: The most instructive record in this file. A moratorium is not a durable fact - in Texas, where counties have thin land-use authority, it survived 24 days once litigation was filed. Any timeline built on a Texas county moratorium should be discounted heavily.
records.source_name: dcmap.us US Data Center Policy Tracker

records.moratorium_note: No county-level moratorium. The City of Peculiar removed the 'data center' definition from its light industrial zoning code in October 2024, which ended Diode Ventures' $1.5B Harper Road Technology Park - a site already sited next to a new Evergy substation and 345 kV lines. Peculiar also ran a 100-day moratorium.
records.board_history: The aftermath is the signal: the city administrator and mayor resigned and an alderman did not stand again. Good power adjacency does not survive a local zoning definition being deleted. Applies to Peculiar, not to the rest of Cass County.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. County commissioners voted against a temporary data center moratorium in 2026 despite the planning board recommending one. Engineered Land Solutions then refiled the rezoning application for Project Delta, the proposed campus at Walnut Cove.
records.board_history: Planning board and commissioners split. Included deliberately as a negative case - a planning board recommendation is not a moratorium, and a refiled application after a rejected moratorium is a live project, not a dead one.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium, and the county overrode the city. Tucson City Council voted 7-0 on 6 August 2025 to end negotiations and halt annexation for Project Blue, the ~290-acre campus. In December 2025 the Pima County Board of Supervisors approved a binding land agreement 3-2 (Scott, Christy, Heinz for; Allen, Cano against), selling roughly 300 acres for about $21M. Construction started April 2026.
records.board_history: City no, county yes, four months apart. The developer simply moved to unincorporated county land. Then in January 2026 opponents sued the county over open meeting law compliance in the approval - the litigation is downstream of the approval, not of the denial.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium and a permissive air regulator. The Shelby County Health Department granted xAI a permit in July 2025 for 15 permanent natural gas turbines totalling 247.2 MW at the Memphis Colossus site, running to 1 January 2027, after more than 1,700 public comments. The Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board then voted 6-1 against the citizens' appeal.
records.board_history: County Commission pushed for a public hearing (5-1 on 26 March 2025, and an 8-3 vote to force the hearing), the Health Department held it starting 25 April 2025, and issued the permit anyway. Shelby County runs its own local air program - the permitting authority here is the county, not TDEC, which is unusual and matters.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. xAI built the Colossus Gas Plant at Southaven with 27 gas turbines totalling about 495 MW to power Colossus 2. Local approval was not the constraint; the federal Clean Air Act was. NAACP and the Mississippi State Conference sued xAI and MZX Tech on 14 April 2026 for operating without an air permit.
records.board_history: The single best illustration of why county posture alone is not a screen. Permissive county, attainment air basin, no moratorium, and the project is in federal court anyway. See ingest/dockets.py - NAACP v. X.AI Corp., 3:26-cv-00074 (N.D. Miss.), cause 42:7413(b).

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. Taylor County signed a tax abatement agreement for the Abilene Stargate campus (Lancium/Crusoe, 1,100 acres, 1.2 GW interconnect fully approved by ERCOT); the City of Abilene granted an 85% property tax discount over 20 years.
records.board_history: Included as the permissive reference point. Texas counties have limited land-use authority outside cities, which is a large part of why the fastest US buildouts are here - the binding constraint moves to ERCOT and TCEQ rather than a board of supervisors.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. Port Washington's Common Council approved the development agreement for Vantage's $15B+ Lighthouse campus on 20 August 2025 - 672 acres, four buildings, roughly 2.5M sq ft, up to 902 MW, for OpenAI and Oracle under Stargate. Ground broken December 2025.
records.board_history: Approved over sustained resident objection at the TID hearings. Permissive municipality inside a permissive county; the Wisconsin cluster (Ozaukee, Racine, Dodge) is the current counterexample to the national moratorium trend.

records.moratorium_note: No moratorium. Microsoft is investing about $20B at Mount Pleasant, on the former Foxconn site in Racine County.
records.board_history: Entered from a single secondary reference in Wisconsin coverage of the 2025 buildout. The permissive posture is well established; the dollar figure and the absence of any restrictive action are the parts to re-verify before relying on this record.
